svg.title: Data and the invoice snapshot
svg.desc: Twenty-one Postgres tables in four groups: tables that make requests safe to repeat and verify, tables for money, rates and caches, tables for clients and follow-up, and tables for the demo and housekeeping. PayPal's invoices are kept as a snapshot in the cache_entries table. A read is answered from the snapshot at once. If the snapshot is older than 60 seconds a refresh runs behind the response: it lists the invoices at PayPal and reads in full only the new or changed ones. A write such as create, send, cancel, a recorded payment or a webhook refreshes the named invoices before it answers.
svg.text: PayPal holds the invoices. Dueline keeps small records and one snapshot.
Highlighted: the snapshot lives here, under one versioned key.
THE INVOICE SNAPSHOT, STALE WHILE REVALIDATE
One list call, then a full
Older than 60 s: refresh behind the answer
A write refreshes its invoices first
A failed refresh keeps the last snapshot

g.text: The route reads the stored snapshot
It answers at once, with due states worked out for today
Older than 60 seconds: a refresh runs behind the answer
Only new or changed invoices are read in full, and the snapshot is saved
A write refreshes the invoices it touched before it answers
